content:
Determinants reward students who spot structure before they expand. One clever row operation can collapse a full 3 by 3 into a single line. Take the free JEE Determinants online test below. It packs 15 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and worked solutions. Push for 12 out of 15, then patch every gap.

What JEE asks from Determinants

  • Expansion of 2 by 2 and 3 by 3 determinants.
  • Row and column operations that simplify a determinant.
  • Cramer rule and the consistency of a linear system.
  • Area of a triangle from three vertex coordinates.
  • Adjoint, inverse and the product property of determinants.
  • Singular matrices and the moment an inverse fails to exist.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Swapping two rows flips the sign of the determinant.
  • Adding a multiple of one row to another leaves it unchanged.
  • The product rule gives determinant of AB as determinant A times determinant B.
  • A unique solution appears when the coefficient determinant stays non zero.
  • Two identical rows force the determinant straight to zero.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Scaling a row and forgetting the determinant scales too.
  • Mixing up the sign pattern while expanding along a row.
  • Treating a zero determinant as proof of no solution.
  • Dropping the modulus in the triangle area formula.

quiz.title: JEE Determinants Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen exam-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Solve 2x + 3y = 7 and 3x + y = 7 by Cramer rule.
questions.explanation: Here D = −7, Dx = −14 and Dy = −7. So x = 2 and y = 1.

questions.q: Assertion (A): AX = 0 has a non-trivial solution if |A| = 0. Reason (R): if |A| ≠ 0, the only solution to AX = 0 is X = 0.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. But R describes the trivial case, so it does not explain the non-trivial one.

questions.q: If the elements of a determinant form an arithmetic progression, its value is:
questions.explanation: Row differences produce two equal rows. Equal rows send the determinant to zero.

questions.q: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with A² = A, then |A| equals:
questions.explanation: Taking determinants gives |A|² = |A|. So |A| is 0 or 1.

questions.q: The determinant with rows (x+1, x−1) and (x−1, x+1) equals:
questions.explanation: The value is (x+1)² − (x−1)², which expands to 4x.

questions.q: If A is an orthogonal matrix, then |A| can be:
questions.explanation: From A·Aᵀ = I we get |A|² = 1. So |A| is plus or minus one.

questions.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 0), (6, 0) and (4, 3).
questions.explanation: The base is 5 and the height is 3. Area = ½ × 5 × 3 = 15/2.

questions.q: For what value of x is the matrix with rows (1−x, 2) and (18, 6−x) singular?
questions.explanation: Set (1−x)(6−x) − 36 = 0. This gives x = −3 or x = 10.

questions.q: If A is an invertible matrix of order 2, then det(A⁻¹) equals:
questions.explanation: Since A·A⁻¹ = I, the determinants multiply to 1. So det(A⁻¹) = 1/det(A).

questions.q: If A is a non-singular 2 × 2 matrix with |A| = 4, then |(adj A)⁻¹| is:
questions.explanation: For order 2, |adj A| = |A| = 4. Its inverse determinant is 1/4.

questions.q: For the system AX = B with |A| ≠ 0, the system has:
questions.explanation: A non-zero determinant makes A invertible. So X = A⁻¹B is the one solution.

questions.q: If |A| = 2 and |B| = 3 for 3 × 3 matrices, then |2AB⁻¹| equals:
If |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O, then AX = B is:
questions.explanation: This is the exact condition for no common solution. So the system is inconsistent.

questions.q: Which row operation changes the value of a determinant?
options: Adding 5 times the first row to the second
Interchanging the first and second rows
Adding the second row to the third
questions.explanation: Row addition keeps the value. Only interchanging two rows flips its sign.

questions.q: Which row operation preserves the value of a determinant?
options: Multiplying a row by a scalar
Adding a multiple of one row to another
questions.explanation: Adding a multiple of one row to another leaves the determinant fixed. The other operations change it.
